forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 25%. Late April 2026 update: Anthropic withheld Claude Mythos 5 from public release as 'too capable to deploy' (first time a frontier lab has withheld a completed model). Meta released Muse Spark (closed) and DeepSeek previewed V4 with 1M-token context. GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1 Pro tied at #1 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index; Gemini 3.1 Pro hit 77.1% on ARC-AGI-2 (more than double Gemini 3 Pro). Median days between frontier releases dropped to 11. Despite striking capability gains, no credible lab has publicly declared AGI achievement, and the term remains contested. ~44 months to resolution.
forecasts.base_rate: ~25% aggregated from Metaculus, Kalshi, expert surveys for AGI by 2029
factors_up: Anthropic withholding Mythos 5 as too capable signals near-AGI (+3pp)
ARC-AGI-2 doubling on Gemini 3.1 Pro to 77.1% (+2pp)
Frontier release cadence accelerating to 11-day median (+2pp)
Hassabis and Altman maintaining 2027-2030 timelines (+2pp)
factors_down: No credible lab has publicly claimed AGI achievement (-4pp)
Definition of AGI remains contested (-3pp)
Resolution window now <44 months (-2pp)
OpenAI revenue miss hints at scaling-economics caution (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether resolution criteria treat near-frontier withheld models as AGI
Whether ARC-AGI-2 progress generalises to economically valuable agentic work
Whether 3+ leading researchers coordinate on a public AGI declaration

update_triggers.up: Major lab publicly declares AGI; 3+ leading researchers endorse a specific milestone; ARC-AGI-2 saturated
update_triggers.down: Stall in frontier capability gains; major labs walk back timelines; capex pullback

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Nudge up from 19% to 20%. April 2026 brought further evidence of AI-driven contraction in consultancy: PwC announced a sweeping consulting overhaul, KPMG UK targeting ~600 cuts (440 audit assistant manager roles + 120 advisory), and 61,000+ AI-driven layoffs across white-collar sectors year-to-date. Big Four 'attrition model' is breaking. ResultSense and CityAM frame this explicitly as an 'AI reckoning'. Still: ≥33% sector-wide value/jobs decline by 2030 is aggressive, requires sustained year-on-year contraction, and partner-led advisory work remains relatively insulated. The threshold also requires '2+ credible analyses' attributing the decline primarily to AI.
forecasts.base_rate: ~10-15% historical base rate for any major professional service sector contracting 33%+ in 6 years; very few precedents
factors_up: PwC announced consulting overhaul (+2pp)
KPMG UK targeting ~600 cuts (+1pp)
61k+ AI-attributed layoffs in Q1 2026 across white-collar (+2pp)
Entry-level consulting postings now require AI skills in 25% of cases (+1pp)
factors_down: Partner-led strategy work remains insulated (-3pp)
Sector-wide 33%+ contraction has few historical precedents (-3pp)
Resolution requires 2+ credible analyses attributing to AI (-2pp)
Big Four pivoting to AI-services revenue offsetting losses (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether consultancy revenue and employment move together or decouple (firms cut jobs while preserving revenue)
Whether AI displacement outpaces graduate hiring slowdown vs. produces net headcount falls
How resolution authorities define 'consultancy' (Big Four vs. boutiques vs. economic consultancy specifically)

update_triggers.up: Big Four announce >15% staff cuts; consultancy revenue contracts y/y in two straight years
update_triggers.down: Big Four headcount and revenue grow in 2026; AI-services revenue offsets analytical losses

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 3%. April 2026 polling continues to show Labour in third place. Electoral Calculus April MRP: Reform 24% (188 seats), Conservatives 21% (159 seats), Labour 17% (86 seats). Ipsos: Reform leads by 6pp; Labour and Conservatives tied at 19%. Combined Lab+Con vote share at 37.1%, down from 57.4% at GE2024. No sign of Labour recovery; Reform consolidating leftward gains in northern metropolitan boroughs. Election can be called any time before December 2029 — Labour's recovery window is theoretically wide but trajectory is downward.
forecasts.base_rate: Governments mid-term rarely fall this far behind without recovery; but recovery from third place with ~17% support at this stage is rare (~5-10% historically)
factors_up: Up to 3.5 years before election can occur (+2pp)
Vote fragmentation could allow Labour to win on low share (+1pp)
Incumbency advantages and access to Downing St communications (+1pp)
factors_down: Labour at 17-19% in MRP polling (-3pp)
Electoral Calculus projects 86 seats — historic low (-3pp)
Reform consolidating northern strongholds (-2pp)
No sign of policy or leadership reset (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Reform-Conservative tactical voting emerges to lock Labour out further
Whether a leadership change in Labour produces a polling bounce
Timing of next election (early call vs running to 2029)

update_triggers.up: Labour recovers to 25%+ in MRP polling; Reform implodes
update_triggers.down: Labour falls below 15%; Reform-Tory pact emerges

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 74%. The April 2026 capability tempo (Mythos 5 withheld, GPT-5.4/Gemini 3.1 Pro at parity, ARC-AGI-2 doubling, 11-day release cadence) is consistent with continued exponential progress. With ~104 months to deadline, probability remains elevated. Key risk to this forecast is not capability stagnation but resolution-criteria adversity (lab unwilling to publicly declare AGI) or definitional drift.
forecasts.base_rate: ~70-75% from aggregated forecasts (Metaculus, Manifold, expert surveys for AGI by 2034-2035)
factors_up: Continued frontier release cadence at 11-day median (+2pp)
Reasoning/agentic benchmark improvements (ARC-AGI-2) (+2pp)
Massive capital deployment (Anthropic raised $25B+$40B from AMZN/GOOG) (+2pp)
104-month resolution window is generous (+2pp)
factors_down: No public AGI declaration to date (-3pp)
Resolution requires explicit announcement, not capability proof (-3pp)
Possible scaling/economics ceilings not yet visible (-2pp)
OpenAI revenue miss may presage capex moderation (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether labs publicly declare 'AGI' even when capabilities reach common operationalisations
Whether scaling laws hold past 10T parameter regime
Whether agentic/autonomous-research milestones trigger researcher consensus

update_triggers.up: Major lab declares AGI; widespread autonomous R&D deployment

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 10%. Late April 2026 brought continued escalation but no kinetic action. AEI's April 24 update notes a two-day PLA exercise revealing a three-phase operational plan, including hypersonic missile deployment and Coast Guard integration. Liaoning carrier task group passage to the Western Pacific signals resolve. Taiwan's MOI conducted first-ever inter-ministerial blockade-response drill (April 14) and is integrating 57 radar stations. Trends point upward but threshold for a >72-hour blockade or assault remains very high; PRC continues grey-zone preference. ~44 months to resolution.
forecasts.base_rate: Historical base rate for major-power initiating cross-strait kinetic operations within 4-year windows: ~3-5%
factors_up: PLA three-phase operational plan revealed (+3pp)
Liaoning task group deployment to Western Pacific (+2pp)
Hypersonic missile deployment in exercises (+1pp)
Trump-Xi diplomacy ambiguity (+1pp)
factors_down: PRC continues preference for grey-zone over kinetic action (-3pp)
Taiwan defensive integration improving (-2pp)
US-Philippines Balikatan signals continued deterrence (-1pp)
44-month window still requires unusually rapid escalation (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether 2027 'Davidson window' translates into action
Whether grey-zone operations cross the 72-hour blockade threshold by accident
Trump administration posture on cross-strait deterrence

update_triggers.up: PLA mobilises reservists; PRC shifts rhetoric from 'reunification' to 'liberation'; large-scale amphibious exercise
update_triggers.down: Cross-strait dialogue resumes; PRC economic problems force military restraint

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. ONS March 2026 CPI at 3.3% (up from 3.0% in February). Drivers: transport (+4.7% YoY), motor fuels, services inflation sticky around 4-5%. April 2026 figures expected 30 April but PwC and other forecasters expect ~3.0-3.4% range. Bank rate held at 3.75-4.0%. With ~8 months of CPI data to come before December 2026, and current rate >150bp above target, falling below 2.0% in any month before January 2027 requires an extraordinary disinflation shock (commodity collapse, sterling appreciation, or recession). Realistic base case: CPI declines toward 2.5% by year-end but does not breach 2.0%.
forecasts.base_rate: Conditional on current CPI 3.3% with rising trajectory, single-month dip below 2% within 8 months: ~2-3%
factors_up: Energy price base effects in autumn 2026 (+1pp)
BoE policy lag could over-tighten and trigger sharp disinflation (+1pp)
factors_down: Current CPI at 3.3% and rising (-3pp)
Services inflation sticky 4-5% (-2pp)
Wage growth still ~5% (-2pp)
BoE forecast does not see sub-2% before mid-2027 (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether energy price shock or commodity collapse provides one-off downside surprise
Whether labour market deterioration accelerates wage disinflation
VAT/regulatory changes in autumn budget

update_triggers.up: CPI prints fall to 2.5% or below by Q3 2026; recession deepens
update_triggers.down: CPI exceeds 4% in any month; services inflation accelerates

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Nudge up from 96% to 97%. Trailer for Spider-Man: Brand New Day surpassed 1 billion views — the first movie trailer in history to do so — and set a new 24-hour record at 718.6 million views (beating Deadpool & Wolverine's mark in just 8 hours, ending at 373 million in 24h per Deadline; Variety reports 718.6M). US release confirmed July 31 2026 (Phase Six MCU; Cretton directing; Holland, Zendaya, Sink, Bernthal, Ruffalo). Box Office Mojo and The Numbers track. With NWH at $1.92B as comparable, $1.5B threshold by 31 Dec 2026 is highly likely.
forecasts.base_rate: MCU sequels with prior franchise grosses over $1.5B exceed $1.5B in opening calendar year ~85-90% of the time; Spider-Man trilogy specifically averages $1.3-1.9B
factors_up: Trailer 1B views — historic record (+3pp)
718.6M views in 24h (record) signals demand (+2pp)
July 31 release preserves full holiday-season runway (+1pp)
Strong cast/director (Holland/Zendaya/Cretton) (+1pp)
factors_down: Reviews/word-of-mouth uncertain pre-release (-1pp)
Competing Q4 tentpoles could compress run (-1pp)
China market access uncertainty (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Critical reception and CinemaScore
China release window and quota allocation
Streaming-cannibalisation dynamics

update_triggers.up: Tracking shows >$300M opening; positive early reviews

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 98%. Latest April 2026 reporting: Anthropic crossed $30B ARR April 7 (gross — disputed by OpenAI which puts comparable net at ~$22B). OpenAI at ~$24B (last public confirmation Feb; reportedly missed internal targets). Combined gross ARR sits at ~$54B today; combined net ~$46B. To reach $70B by Q4 2026, sector needs ~30% growth over 8 months — well below current trajectories (Anthropic tripled in 4 months; OpenAI ARR expected to reach ~$30-40B by year-end per Bloomberg/The Information). Resolution criterion uses 'most recent credible reporting', which would normally accept reported gross figures.
forecasts.base_rate: Conditional on $54B gross combined and growth trajectories: 95-99%
factors_up: Anthropic at $30B and tripling 4-monthly (+1pp)
OpenAI confirmed $24B with continued growth (+1pp)
Resolution accepts reported ARR (gross or net) (+1pp)
Q4 enterprise contracts typically lift both firms (+1pp)
factors_down: OpenAI missed internal Q1 targets (-1pp)
Accounting dispute could complicate clean reporting (-1pp)
Macro/capex pullback risk (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether resolution authority uses gross or net Anthropic figure
Whether OpenAI growth re-accelerates or stalls
Whether either company changes ARR disclosure cadence

update_triggers.down: Both companies pause or reduce ARR disclosure; major enterprise pullback

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Trim from 43% to 42%. OBR March 2026 EFO: GDP averages 1.6% across 2027-2030; productivity growth assumed 1.0% medium-term, but TFP revised down to 0.8% (vs 1.1% prior). Upside scenario (productivity rebounds to 1.5%) lifts GDP nearer 2%; downside scenario (productivity stalls at 0.5%) drags GDP toward 1.0%. IPPR and IFS commentary highlights navigating-narrow-paths uncertainty. AI productivity dividend remains a wildcard — partly upside, partly disinflationary on labour share. Central case sits just below 1.5% threshold, hence near-coin-flip with downside skew.
forecasts.base_rate: UK 10-year GDP averages: 1950s-2010s decadal averages span 1.3%-3.0%; ~50% of decades exceed 1.5%
factors_up: AI productivity dividend (Microsoft/MIT studies) (+5pp)
Population growth via net migration (~250k/yr baseline) (+3pp)
Capital-deepening from data-centre/infra investment (+2pp)
factors_down: OBR TFP revised down to 0.8% medium-term (-3pp)
Demographic ageing (-3pp)
Net-zero transition costs front-loaded into 2030s (-3pp)
Trade policy fragmentation drag (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Magnitude and timing of AI productivity dividend
Net migration policy through 2030s
Whether housing-supply reform delivers planning-driven productivity gains

update_triggers.up: OBR/BoE upgrade medium-term productivity assumption to 1.2%+; AI revenue evidence in productivity statistics
update_triggers.down: OBR cuts productivity assumption further; recession in late 2020s
